gloss: start of summer; first day of summer (solar term)

definitions.gloss: start of summer; beginning of summer (solar term)
definitions.explanation: One of the 24 solar terms (二十四節気) in the traditional East Asian calendar. Falls around May 5-6 in the modern calendar, marking the traditional beginning of summer.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{立夏|りっか}だ。
examples.english: Today is the start of summer.

examples.japanese: {立夏|りっか}を{過|す}ぎると{日差|ひざ}しが{強|つよ}くなる。
examples.english: After the start of summer, the sunlight gets stronger.

examples.japanese: {暦|こよみ}の{上|うえ}では{立夏|りっか}を{迎|むか}えたが、まだ{肌寒|はだざむ}い{日|ひ}が{続|つづ}いている。
examples.english: Although the calendar says summer has begun, the chilly days continue.

notes:
One of the 24 solar terms ({二十四節気|にじゅうしせっき}) that divide the year based on the sun's position. {立夏|りっか} falls around May 5-6 each year and marks the traditional beginning of summer, though actual temperatures in Japan at this time are still mild.

THE FOUR "BEGINNING" SOLAR TERMS:
- {立春|りっしゅん}: start of spring (~February 4)
- {立夏|りっか}: start of summer (~May 5)
- {立秋|りっしゅう}: start of autumn (~August 7)
- {立冬|りっとう}: start of winter (~November 7)

FORMS:
{立|りつ} (to stand, to begin) + {夏|か} (summer)

USAGE:
Often appears in weather forecasts and seasonal greetings. The phrase {暦|こよみ}の{上|うえ}では{立夏|りっか} ("according to the calendar it's the start of summer") acknowledges that the astronomical date doesn't always match actual weather conditions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {立夏|りっか}を{迎|むか}える: to reach the start of summer
- {立夏|りっか}の{候|こう}: seasonal greeting for early May
